critiques.summary: Group 0 final gate (13 routes). Checked the final-gate-2 captures, all JSON logs, and a fresh live run with states and measure (shots/final-gate-critic-0/live, 52 captures). Every capture came back HTTP 200 with 0 console errors, 0 failed requests, 0 unresolved vars, 0 off-palette colours, no horizontal overflow and max CLS 0.0117. The only non-Octicons are the gitea, feishu and matrix brand logos in the Add Webhook menu, which fall under the documented exception. In both schemes the header, UnderlineNav, NavList, Box, buttons, overlays and diffs are Primer-accurate. wiki-page and pr-commits-tab measure identical to github.com, e.g. New page 75.5x28 at 12px/500 with #1f883d. Nothing in this group reads as recoloured Gitea. Scores range from 8 to 9. The lowest are commit-detail and compare-two-tags at 8, because their header and commits structure comes from Gitea's templates and differs from GitHub's. There are no blockers or majors. The minors are: an unstyled current page in the feed pagination (navigation); octicon-file-code where GitHub uses octicon-code on commit rows (icons); a settings NavList with no leading icons or group headings; and the commit and compare header structure. Everything else is a nit. Full report: /Users/michael/work/gitea/gitea-theme-github/docs/critiques/final-gate-group-0.md; crops are in /Users/michael/work/gitea/gitea-theme-github/shots/final-gate-critic-0/.

critiques.summary:
I reviewed all 13 routes in both schemes at 1440 and 390, top to bottom via crops in /Users/michael/work/gitea/gitea-theme-github/shots/final-gate-critic-1/. I compared them against docs/reference where a reference exists, and re-ran shoot.mjs with --measure --states into shots/final-gate-critic-1/live (theme github-auto, admin theme untouched). The full report is in /Users/michael/work/gitea/gitea-theme-github/docs/critiques/final-gate-group-1.md.

Audit logs are clean on all 52 captures: 0 unresolved vars, 0 off-palette colours, 0 non-Octicon icons, 0 unlayered CSS, no horizontal overflow, max CLS 0.0029. The only console errors are the expected 404 and third-party badges (shields.io, dependabot-badges) that the shoot tool blocks. Sampled pixels match Primer in both schemes.

Pages with a github.com equivalent come very close:
- repo-home-readme: page height 10829 vs 10886, and the README column matches the reference to the pixel.
- pr-conversation, actions-list, org-members: score 8.5.
- Settings and admin pages read as native Primer: 9.

Two major issues:
1. **README header wraps at 390 (code).** A mobile rule in src/code/file-view.css (~line 284), `.file-header .file-header-left { flex: 1 0 100% }`, was meant for the file view but also hits the repo-home README header. The pencil drops to a second row on every repo home.
2. **Branches page structure (pages/repo).** It lacks GitHub's page title, UnderlineNav and table header row, and shows 5 inline icon buttons per row where GitHub has trash plus a kebab.

Minor issues:
- Mobile repo home puts the whole sidebar before the README (pages/repo).
- Emoji-led descriptions wrap onto their own line in flex item-body rows at 390 (data-display).
- The 404 page is a generic blankslate with no search field (data-display).
- The Actions page lacks its title and filter input (template).
- A stray hamburger shows on logged-out auth pages (navigation).
- The forgot-password message has no container (pages/auth).

Remaining findings are nits: title-case locale strings, Mermaid theme, flash icon wrap, row alignment.

Scores (light/dark/390):
- 9/9/8.5 — site-admin-config, user-settings-account, user-settings-orgs
- 9/9/8 — repo-home-markdown-showcase-playground, repo-home-readme-with-images-and-tables
- 8.5/8.5/8.5 — pr-conversation-closed-unmerged, actions-list, org-members, org-projects
- 8.5/8.5/8 — explore-repos
- 8/8/8 — branches, forgot-password
- 7/7/7 — not-found

Group 3 final-gate review of 13 routes. I read all 52 captures in final-gate-2, cropping each full page including the lower parts, and compared them with the github.com references where they exist (repo-issue, releases, issues-list-closed; login used as the auth yardstick). I also ran a fresh live run with states and measurements into shots/final-gate-critic-3/live: 52 pages, 0 problems. The logs are clean on every route. There are no console errors or failed requests, no unresolved variables, no off-palette colours and no horizontal overflow, and max CLS is 0.0132. The only non-Octicon icon is gitea-npm, an allowed brand exception. Measured metrics match github.com: heading 32/400, underline-nav items 75×30, primary button 93×32, markdown 14/21, auth input and button 352×40. The PR diff colours are exact Primer values in both schemes. Dark mode is at parity with light everywhere; no dark-only defects were found.

Two majors:
1. releases: the desktop layout keeps the classic left column (tag, commit, Compare), while current github.com uses a Release list nav with tag, commit and Compare inside the card. Our own 390 layout already does that reorder. Owner: pages/repo.
2. repo-create: the form sits in a boxed card with a gray header, while github.com/new is an unboxed page with a Subhead-style heading. Owner: pages/repo.

Notable minors:
- The markdown composer is styled only inside issue/PR forms, so the admin banner, release and wiki editors look like stock Gitea. Owner: controls (the rules live in pages/issues-prs/composer.css today).
- Merge-style menu items are 54px tall. Owner: pages/issues-prs.
- Mobile layout problems: toggles wrap under their labels on admin config; the admin heading is squeezed to 3 lines; full-bleed file boxes keep rounded corners; nav rows are cut off with no overflow affordance.
- A lone hamburger floats on the auth page.

Scores range from 7.5 (releases desktop, repo-create) to 9 (issues-list-closed). Most routes are at 8.5, i.e. they match github.com with nits.

critiques.summary:
Group 6 passes the gate. There are no blockers or majors. Every route scores 8.0 to 9.0 on desktop and 7.5 to 8.5 on mobile. Audit data is clean on all 12 routes, both schemes and both widths: 0 unresolved vars, 0 off-palette colours, no horizontal overflow, CLS at or below 0.0085. The only non-Octicons are brand marks (webhook types, npm). The fresh live run (--measure --states, shots/final-gate-critic-6/live) logged 0 console errors and 0 failed requests. The 21 errors on repo-home in final-gate-2 are third-party README images the shoot tool blocks, not theme defects.

- **Closest to github.com:** repo-home, repo-pull-files, wiki-home and pr-commits-tab-playground. The diff colours and file header in repo-pull-files match github.com pixel-for-pixel in both schemes.
- **Main minor issues:** the README box header on repo-home (bg-muted, 8px inset instead of GitHub's white tab header), on project-board the last column is clipped at 1440 and the columns stop at a fixed height, the issue page container is 8px wider than the rest of the site, and the webhooks empty state doesn't look like a Primer Blankslate.
- **Mobile weak spots:** blame drops the date from its group headers and its toolbar wraps into three rows. Comment headers leave an orphan 'ago' on its own line. The underline nav puts the active-tab bar under the '…' overflow button.

Report: /Users/michael/work/gitea/gitea-theme-github/docs/critiques/final-gate-group-6.md. Crops and live captures: /Users/michael/work/gitea/gitea-theme-github/shots/final-gate-critic-6/.

Group 7 is technically clean. Across all 48 JSON logs there are no console errors, no failed requests, no unresolved vars, no off-palette colours, no non-Octicon icons and no horizontal overflow; the largest CLS is 0.004. Sampled dark pixels match github.com exactly (#0d1117, #151b23, #3d444d). The best routes score 8.5–9: wiki-page-list, repo-issues, repo-commits, pr-conversation-open, user-profile-stars-tab, org-settings and site-admin. Three routes pull the group down. blame-playground-multiple-authors is 7.5 because it has no blame age heat strip or Older/Newer legend; Gitea sends no age data, so CSS cannot add them. org-settings-labels is 7.5 because its empty state is not a Primer Blankslate: a bare select spanning 3 italic lines plus centred muted text. package-versions is 7.5 because the page has no title and the version name is not a link. The main problem across routes is on mobile: underline-nav.css hides the tab icons below 768/1200px and the '…' overflow button gets the active underline, while the github.com 390 references keep the icons. Settings NavLists also have no leading Octicons.
